title: Using the TypeScript Playground knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the role of TypeScript in a development workflow?
options: It validates all network data automatically.
It removes the need for runtime tests.
It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
It replaces the JavaScript runtime in every browser.
questions.answer_key: It checks types and improves tooling; the application still runs as JavaScript in its selected runtime.
questions.explanation: Type checking is a development-time layer and does not replace runtime verification.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Using the TypeScript Playground”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with writing and editing typescript online and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with writing and editing typescript online and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Writing and editing TypeScript online”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Using the TypeScript Playground”?
options: Check inspecting compiler output, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume testing isolated type-system examples is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check inspecting compiler output, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Inspecting compiler output”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
